runs.narrative: This commit does what its message says: it removes the hardcoded dead Render.com address (`https://medrecord-api.onrender.com/v1`) from the app's authentication module and instead pulls the shared API base URL from the existing api-client file, so all four login-related network calls (send code, verify code, verify patient code, refresh token) now point at whatever server the demo startup script configures. The diff matches the description closely — it is a small, consistent one-line-style change across those four functions, plus a routine update to the project's tracking/status document. The claim that the calls will now honor the environment-set tunnel URL depends on the api-client file's behavior, which isn't included in this diff, but nothing here contradicts it. No testing is claimed in the commit message, and in fact the tracking-doc update explicitly hands the next step to a device tester to run the demo and confirm on-device login works, so verification is still outstanding; that keeps this at code-complete rather than tested. One minor note for a developer's awareness: the merged pull request's description talks about an ngrok tunnel while this commit and the status doc describe a switch to cloudflared, and the status doc's "Last Updated" date is moved backward from 2026-06-23 to 2026-06-22 — these look like housekeeping/chronology artifacts rather than problems with the code change itself. This commit swaps the demo backend's public tunnel from Cloudflare's cloudflared service over to a free ngrok account with a fixed, permanent web address (lunchbox-saddled-relock.ngrok-free.dev), because the Cloudflare "named tunnel" option turned out to require a paid domain. The startup script (scripts/start-demo.sh) was rewritten to launch ngrok against that fixed domain instead of scraping a fresh random Cloudflare URL each run, and it now stops with a clear error if the domain isn't configured; this script change is self-contained and matches what the message describes. The message also explains that an earlier note claiming "ngrok breaks TLS" was re-diagnosed as ngrok's free-tier browser-warning page, which is bypassed by sending an "ngrok-skip-browser-warning" header on each request. The author reports checking the backend, tunnel, and a curl request end to end with a 200 OK response; I can see testing commands referenced in the governance audit log but did not run anything myself to confirm that outcome. Two follow-up items are explicitly still open and routed to a different agent: adding the same header to the frontend API code (src/api/apiClient.ts) and re-verifying the flow on a real device. The remaining changed files are routine project bookkeeping — the status document plus the agent-ownership registry and audit log. No story or issue was attributed to this commit, and none is needed: it is a self-contained infrastructure change whose purpose is clear from the message and diff. It is marked Code complete rather than Tested because the required on-device verification is still pending. Follow-up for the developer: when/how will this be tested, and what's the ETA?

The diff builds the header once and applies it to both network paths in that function — the plain fetch fallback used under Expo Go and the certificate-pinned path — while still letting caller-supplied headers override it, which matches what the message describes. The message also says every API call in the app funnels through this one function (covering apiClient, auth, and consent), but the diff only touches `pinnedFetch` itself, so that broader architectural claim can't be confirmed from this change alone. The message states the fix was checked with curl and a Node fetch smoke test; I have only read the message and diff and did not run anything, and the message is explicit that real on-device testing has not been done and has been routed to the device tester — so this is code-complete rather than tested. The commit also updates a project-state document and an agent activity log, which is the routine tracking this repo's commits normally carry alongside a change. No story or issue was attributed to this commit, and since it is a self-contained infrastructure fix, none is needed. The pull request that later bundles this work describes on-device verification as complete, but that reflects the aggregate state at merge time across multiple commits, not this commit on its own. Follow-up for the developer: when/how will this be tested, and what's the ETA?

The diff supports what the message describes: a new screen file implementing three display states (an idle state with a number pad and a "how it works" hint, a "found" state showing a patient card with a "Request Consent" button, and a "not found" state with options to register the patient or retry), the screen wired into the app's navigation in App.tsx, and a developer-only shortcut link added to the existing Patient Search screen so the team can reach the mockup during development. The tracking note added to the project state document says the change compiles with zero type errors and was pushed to the dev branch, and it lists a Persona Critic review as the next step; I have only read the commit's message and diff and did not run the type check or the app myself. No formal or on-device testing is claimed for this commit, which is why it reads as code complete rather than tested. A story (D7) was attributed and the work matches it. The pull request attached here is about an unrelated dev-to-main merge and does not conflict with this commit. Follow-up for the developer: when/how will this be tested, and what's the ETA?

This commit addresses a startup deadlock in the medrecord agent-governance system: the file-ownership gate script had no exception for the write that creates the session's agent-marker file, so every new session's first action was blocked because it required an agent to already be declared before the write that declares one could go through. The actual code change adds a small bootstrap exception mirroring one the companion agent-gate script already had, and that three-line change is consistent with what the message describes. The message also says the fix was checked against a simulated cold start and against a Bash-redirect bypass attempt that stayed blocked; I can't independently confirm that from what I was given, since the diff shows only the code change and no test run or output, so that verification should be read as described rather than evidenced. The main reason I'm flagging this is that the diff bundles in a standalone LinkedIn-style article (linkedin-article-hook-governance-deadlock.md) written to be published and read outside the codebase, alongside the code fix. Even though the article covers the same bug, a shareable write-up isn't part of implementing the fix, so this commit mixes unrelated content types; consider splitting it into a code commit and a separate content commit for traceability. Separately and more minor, the ownership-registry file was reformatted and also gained entries for a couple of files and paths the message doesn't call out. No story or issue was attributed to this commit, and none is needed here since its purpose stands on its own as a self-contained infrastructure fix.
